Definition: a Maakathite, or inhabitant of Maakah
BiblicalUsage: The Maakathites were the people of Maakah, a small kingdom east of Jordan, and they held their land when Israel took the country around them. Moses gave their territory to the half tribe of Manasseh, Joshua lists their border among the unconquered lands, and a Maakathite named Eliphelet stood among David's mighty men.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Maakathites show that God keeps peoples the conquerors pass by, and a small kingdom can outlast an empire. I hold that the one Maakathite among David's mighty men is proof that God draws His servants from every nation, not only from Israel.
